title: Catalyst
content: Catalyst is a substance that alters the rate of a chemical reaction but remains chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction.
e: A catalyst changes the rate of a reaction but is chemically the same at the end. It is not written as a consumed reactant in the overall equation.

title: Positive catalyst
content: Positive catalyst is a catalyst that increases the rate of a chemical reaction.
e: A positive catalyst increases the rate of a reaction. It lowers the activation energy by opening a new path.

title: Negative catalyst
content: Negative catalyst is a catalyst that decreases the rate of a chemical reaction.
e: A negative catalyst decreases the rate of a reaction. It gets in the way of the usual path so fewer successful collisions happen.

title: Phase
content: Phase is a portion of a physical state (solid, liquid, gas) that is homogeneous throughout, and can be separated physically from other phases.
e: A phase is a uniform chunk of solid, liquid, or gas that you can physically separate from other phases. Ice floating on water is two phases.

title: Homogeneous catalyst
content: Homogeneous catalyst is a catalyst which is in the same phase as the reactants in a catalyzed reaction.
e: A homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants. Acid catalysing a reaction in aqueous solution is this type.

title: Heterogeneous catalyst
content: Heterogeneous catalyst is a catalyst which is in a different phase from the reactants in a catalysed reaction.
e: A heterogeneous catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants. Iron in the Haber process is a solid catalyst with gaseous reactants.

title: Enzymes
content: Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts for specific biochemical reactions.
e: Enzymes are proteins that catalyse specific biochemical reactions. Each enzyme has a shape that fits its own substrate.

title: Photochemical reaction
content: Photochemical reaction is a chemical reaction initiated by the absorption of energy in the form of light, resulting in specific products.
e: A photochemical reaction starts when a molecule absorbs light. Photosynthesis and the reaction of chlorine with methane in sunlight are this kind of change.

title: Activation energy
content: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy that reacting particles must have to form the activated complex and lead to a reaction.
e: Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles must have to form the activated complex. Below that barrier, they just bounce apart.

title: Transition state
content: Transition state (also known as an intermediate state) is a highly energetic state that would be highly unstable.
e: The transition state is a highly energetic, unstable arrangement on the way from reactants to products. You cannot bottle it; it exists only at the top of the energy barrier.

title: Collision theory
content: Collision theory states that a chemical reaction only takes place when two reacting molecules collide in the correct orientation with sufficient kinetic energy.
e: Collision theory says a reaction happens only if molecules collide with the right orientation and with enough kinetic energy. Miss either condition and you get no product from that hit.

title: Successful collision
content: Successful collision is a collision that causes a chemical reaction.
e: A successful collision is one that actually causes a chemical reaction. The particles hit with enough energy and the correct orientation.

title: Activated complex
content: Activated complex is a temporary unstable arrangement of atoms that may form products or break apart to reform the reactants.
e: The activated complex is a temporary, unstable arrangement of atoms at the energy peak. It can split forward to products or fall back to reactants.
